name: Menstrual cups (silicone/latex/other polymers)
native_basis: mucosal material-content — total heavy-metal content of the finished article per unit mass, as placed on market (device basis; vulvovaginal mucosal and, for internal devices, prolonged internal contact). Not a dermal basis and not a leachate/migration number.
exposure_pathway: Vulvovaginal mucosal (more permeable and bioavailable than intact skin) and, for internal devices, prolonged internal contact
components: cup body, stem, and any pigment/colorant masterbatch — silicone cups additionally screened for residual organotin condensation-cure catalyst (tin)
supplementary_leachables: Antimony (Sb) is monitored as a supplementary leachable on PET and polymer components (PET polycondensation uses an antimony-trioxide catalyst that leaches under prolonged contact; marcelis2024 measured antimony in intimate products). Sb is OUTSIDE the 10-analyte HMTc certification panel; its inclusion for polymer intimate devices is logged as a Step-0 panel-governance question.

Pb.rationale: Lead is present in this device class per routed occurrence evidence (nic-corcrain2025 (Pb, tAs leached across tampons, pads, cups and period underwear into simulated vaginal fluid); marcelis2024 (full-panel screen incl. Al and Sn across tampons, pads, cups and other intimate products)); no jurisdiction sets a Lead content limit for a menstrual or intimate-care device (medical-device law governs ISO 10993 biocompatibility, not content). The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material — a not-material determination would be contradicted by the occurrence evidence and would fail the substantiation gate.
Pb.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with component-level sampling of the finished article (cup body, stem, and any pigment/colorant masterbatch — silicone cups additionally screened for residual organotin condensation-cure catalyst (tin)). No sovereign sets a heavy-metal content limit for this device form, so no fixed numeric ceiling is published; any lot result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA tightening against the tightest available context + supplier corrective action). Lead is material for this device (an intravaginal polymer device with prolonged mucosal contact; measured in cups in the routed corpus).
Pb.materiality_basis: nic-corcrain2025 (Pb, tAs leached across tampons, pads, cups and period underwear into simulated vaginal fluid); marcelis2024 (full-panel screen incl. Al and Sn across tampons, pads, cups and other intimate products)

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic; no jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any feminine-care product. It is governed by reflex speciation: whenever total arsenic is elevated, inorganic arsenic is speciated by HPLC-ICP-MS, and the inorganic fraction is held under ALARA.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation triggered by an elevated total-arsenic screen.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury forms by microbial methylation in aquatic food webs and bioaccumulates in fish muscle; a cellulose/polymer intimate device has no methylation pathway and no dietary mercury source. Intimate-product metal surveys measure TOTAL mercury, not methylmercury, so no routed source reports methylmercury (the not-material integrity gate is speciation-aware). Any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury control/ceiling. No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a menstrual or intimate-care product.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No MeHg ML for any menstrual/intimate-care product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury MLs are scoped to fish and seafood only.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: 21 CFR 884 & EU MDR 2017/745 (device biocompatibility, no content ML); Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, ASEAN 2019, Korea MFDS 2024/2025, FDA 21 CFR 700 (cosmetic contaminant limits — none set MeHg)

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Device forms carry no sovereign heavy-metal content limit, so every panel cell resolves to a mandatory analytical control or a substantiated not-material determination; no occurrence percentile is computed and no number is invented. Cosmetic forms read across the strictest sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic contaminant limit. Two basis families (device content, cosmetic content) are never conflated, and neither is a leachate/migration number. Provenance vocabulary: {regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet}.
lineage_note: Initial Cat-15 Feminine Care government-limit standard (HMTc Method v2.0). Flagship mucosal-exposure category. Device subcategories (tampons, pads, cups, discs, period underwear, other) carry no sovereign heavy-metal content limit (medical-device law governs ISO 10993 biocompatibility, not content) and resolve to mandatory control on every occurrence- or pathway-established metal (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Cr, Sn, Al; iAs and Cr-VI reflex-speciation controls); methylmercury is the sole not-material cell (no biological methylation pathway; bounded by the total-mercury control). Cosmetic subcategories (feminine wipes, deodorants, douches, intimate washes) read across the German BVL 2017 sovereign cosmetic contaminant limits, adopting the mucosal-contact (toothpaste) tier for lead (500 vs the general-cosmetic 2000 ug/kg) because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa those limits were written for; Cd/tAs/tHg bind the strictest general-cosmetic value (100/500/100), nickel the only sovereign cosmetic Ni limit (Korea MFDS 2025 = 10000). Materiality anchored to shearston2024, ica2024, ellison2026, carlin2020, nic-corcrain2025, marcelis2024. Direction: toward the literature (CLAUDE.md Part 2/19).
